capitals.name: Blois
capitals.note: The page: the county was 'centred on Blois' and the first Frankish county's 'capital city was already in Blois'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Blois before 990. The page: the title 'was formally created in 832' for William, son of Adrian, who governed Blois as count of Orleans; the county was 'centred on Blois'. No boundary on the page: a 25 km radius around Blois is my reading (confidence 2). Infobox gives no area.

correction.text: Blois with Tours, Chartres and Châteaudun under Theobald I

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page says Blois passed to Theobald I 'around 940' and that he was also count of Tours, Chartres and Châteaudun; the 990 Cliopatria shape (48 cells, 11,218 km2) holds exactly these (Blois, Chartres, Châteaudun, Touraine). The page does not date the three additions (confidence 1 in the ledger).

11,218 km2; infobox gives no area. Odo II was 'count of Blois, Chartres, Châteaudun, Champagne, Beauvais and Tours from 1004' (Odo II page); Champagne is Cliopatria's own County of Champagne shape until 1027, so this shape rightly holds the Loire counties. Odo was beaten by Fulk III of Anjou and Herbert I of Maine at Pontlevoy in July 1016; no page opened gives a border change. Valid for 990-1021; keyframe county-of-blois_1022 adds Champagne from 1022.

After Stephen I's death in 1019/1020 Odo 'seized Troyes, Meaux and all of Champagne for himself without royal approval'; the page dates his titles of count of Troyes and Meaux to 1022 (the Blois page says Meaux 'by 1019' and Troyes 'in 1023'; the Champagne page says 1021). Cliopatria adds Champagne to the Blois shape only in 1028. Confidence 2 for the year.

38,686 km2 (170 cells): the 990 shape plus Champagne's own 123 cells. 'He was the first to unite Blois and Champagne under one authority.' In 1032 Odo invaded the Kingdom of Burgundy on the death of Rudolph III and retreated before a coalition of Conrad II and Henry I; no border change.

38,821 km2 (171 cells). Valid 1034-1036 only: Odo II died at Bar-le-Duc on 15 November 1037 and his sons divided the domains (keyframes county-of-blois_1037 and _1044 supersede from 1037). Infobox gives no area. Cliopatria keeps all of Champagne in the Blois shape to 1045 while drawing Champagne separately from 1040. Confidence 2: the outline of Champagne is the Cliopatria Champagne shape.

33,026 km2. 7,796 km2. Theobald V (to 1191), Louis I (1191-1205), both counts of Blois and Chartres (Chartres page). The page opened gives no border event.

Cliopatria's Kingdom of France shape of 1402 holds 14 of the 15 cells, so the row ends in 1401 because the county falls into the Orleans appanage and the royal shape. The seat is added back.

ledger.note: 832: Louis the Pious creates the county of Blois. The page: 'the title was formally created in 832, when King Louis the Pious made Adrian's second son count' (William, d. 834). The page gives Blois, not a boundary.

c. 940: Theobald I holds Tours, Chartres and Châteaudun with Blois. The page says Blois passed to him 'around 940' and that 'he was also count of Tours, Chartres and Châteaudun'; it does not date the three counties, so the year bridges a silence.

region.text: Troyes, Meaux and all of Champagne

ledger.note: 1022: Odo II takes Champagne. After Stephen I's death in 1019/1020 he 'seized Troyes, Meaux and all of Champagne for himself without royal approval'; his titles of count of Troyes and Meaux are dated 1022. The pages disagree (Blois: Meaux by 1019, Troyes 1023; Champagne: 1021).

minus.text: Provins and Château-Thierry, the Champagne lands Theobald III kept in 1037

ledger.note: 1037: Odo II dies and Stephen II takes Troyes, Meaux and Vitry. 'In 1037 he took advantage of Conrad II's absence in Italy to invade the Duchy of Lorraine' and died in the rout at Bar-le-Duc on 15 November 1037 (Odo II page); 'his brother Stephen inherited the counties of Meaux, Troyes and Vitry-le-François' (Theobald III page). Theobald III kept Provins, Château-Thierry and St. Florentin.

1044: Geoffrey Martel takes Touraine at Nouy. 'They met in battle at Nouy and Theobald was captured'; he gave up Touraine to regain his freedom. Blois page: 'the county of Tours was definitively lost in 1044 after the Battle of Nouy'.

1063: Theobald III reunites Blois and Champagne. The page: the divided domains were 'reunited in 1063'. The Theobald III page says he used his nephew's absence 'to gain control over Odo's possessions in Champagne', with no year.

1089: Blois and Champagne divided again. 'Following Theobald's death in 1089, Philip I, King of France, was able to arrange for Blois and Champagne' to be divided between Theobald's sons; Stephen-Henry became count of Blois and Chartres in 1089 (Stephen page); Hugh received Champagne after Odo died in 1093.

1125: Theobald IV of Blois becomes Count of Champagne. He is 'count of Champagne and of Brie as Theobald II from 1125' (Theobald II page); Hugh of Troyes is listed 1102-1125 in the Champagne infobox. The pages do not say how the succession passed.

region.text: Champagne, occupied by the royal army

ledger.note: 1142: Louis VII's war on Theobald II of Champagne begins. The page says the conflict 'lasted two years (1142-1144)', with Champagne occupied by the royal army and Vitry-le-François captured; the burning of the church of Vitry killed 1,500 people.
1144: the war with Louis VII ends. The page gives the span 1142-1144 and mentions no treaty.
1152: Theobald IV dies (10 January 1152, Theobald II page) and his lands divide. 'Theobald IV bequeaths Champagne to his elder Henry I and Blois to his younger brother Theobald V.'
1230: the Avesnes branch takes the county. 'The Avesnes branch held the county from 1230 to 1241' (Mary, Countess of Blois); same state, new house.
1241: Blois-Châtillon takes the county and holds it 'until 1397'; the page gives no year for the start of the Châtillon counts, 1241 follows the end of the Avesnes years.

1286: Joan, Countess of Blois, sells Chartres. 'In 1286, she sold the county of Chartres to Philip IV of France.' The Crown lands page also has a '1284: purchase of the County of Chartres' entry and, in 1286, the crown buys it 'from Jeanne of Blois-Châtillon'. Cliopatria draws the loss in 1294.

ledger.counterpart: Châteaudun (holder not named by the pages opened)
ledger.note: 1294: Châteaudun leaves the Blois shape. No page opened says why or to whom (the Châteaudun page is silent; it calls the town the capital of the County of Dunois in the Middle Ages, undated); the year rests on Cliopatria's 1294 shape.

1397: Blois passes from the Châtillon counts to the Duke of Orleans. 'Count Guy II gave up his domain to Duke Louis I of Orléans'; Blois-Châtillon held the county 'until 1397'; Louis I was 'Count of Blois from 1397 to 1407' (Louis I page). The Chartres page says Guy sold the inheritance in 1391, but the Crown lands page agrees with the Blois page: 'In 1397 Guy II sold the county to Louis I of Orléans'; the county stays one state.

1401: Cliopatria's Blois row ends. The pages opened give no event for 1401: the county lasted to 1660 as an Orleans appanage (Blois page infobox) and Cliopatria draws its cells as Kingdom of France from 1402.

wars.outcome: Odo invaded Lorraine in 1037 and died in the rout at Bar-le-Duc, defeated by Gothelo I, on 15 November 1037; his domains were divided between Theobald III and Stephen II.

wars.outcome: Geoffrey Martel besieged Tours; at Nouy Theobald III was captured and gave up Touraine to regain his freedom.
wars.note: The page dates only 1044 ('By 1044, ... besieging Tours').

notes: Not settled. (1) Start 832 (page: title created 832); Cliopatria starts 990, so 832-989 are two new keyframes (Blois pagus; then the four Loire counties from c. 940, confidence 1). (2) Cliopatria's Blois shapes 1028-1045, 1066-1110, 1126-1151 are Blois plus Champagne's own shape. The pages say Champagne was Blois's only 1022-1037, 1063-1089 and 1125-1152 (personal union); new keyframes 1037, 1044, 1063, 1089 correct the 1034 and 1085 rows. Cliopatria also draws a separate Champagne from 1040-1065 and 1094 on, overlapping. The pages disagree on the first union: 1019 (Meaux), 1021 (Champagne page), 1022 (Odo II page), 1023 (Troyes, Blois page). (3) Provins and Château-Thierry (Theobald III page, 1037) are drawn as Blois lands 1037-1062 with a radius; their later fate is on no page. (4) Chartres was sold in 1286 (Chartres page) but Cliopatria removes it in 1294; Châteaudun leaves in 1294 on no page (confidence 1). (5) 1391 (Chartres page) against 1397 (Blois and Louis I pages) for the Orleans purchase of Blois; the county then belonged to the Duke of Orleans to 1498 and to 1660 as an appanage. The dossier ends in 1401 because Cliopatria does; a gap-filler may extend it. (6) No full list of counts was on the pages, so identity.rulers is left out. (7) The Odo II page lists Odo II as count of 'Beauvais' as well; the Blois page does not name Beauvais and no other page confirms it. (8) Gazetteer names needed: Blois, Chartres, Châteaudun, Provins, Château-Thierry (places). Counterparts: county-of-champagne, county-of-anjou, kingdom-of-the-franks, west-franks exist; duchy-of-lorraine exists. The Cliopatria Blois row lacks Sancerre, which the Theobald III page lists among Theobald's counties.
